raw_case_text:
On 24 May 2021, a 51-year-old woman was admitted to our hospital with a 1-week history of fever. She developed a fever of 39.5 C with chills that lasted for about 20-30 min as well as cough, headaches, sweating, and fatigue. The patient was evaluated in an emergency department 5 days previous to the presentation. On examination, blood analysis demonstrated normal white blood cell counts (4.25 x 109/L) and neutrophil percentage (63.7%), and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP, 8.66 mg/L) with chest computed tomography (CT) within normal limits. The patient was treated with ceftriaxone (2g qd ivgtt) for 2 days but body temperatures remained elevated (>39-40 C) and other clinical symptoms also persisted. The patient was admitted for hospitalization.
The patient's history indicated that she was a farmer and worked with sheep. The patient reported no previous history of symptoms and was not on medication that could cause symptoms. Other family members did not report similar symptoms. Physical examination was within normal limits. Laboratory results indicated significant elevations of CRP and serum amyloid protein A (SAA) and moderate to minor elevations of D-dimer, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, adenosine deaminase, creatinine, procalcitonin (PCT), and hepatitis B surface antibody (Table 1).
At admission, electrocardiograms (ECGs) showed a heart rate (HR) of only 74 beats per minute (bpm) with sinus rhythm despite a body temperature of 39.1 C. The ECG demonstrated no arrhythmia, shortening of the PR segment, ST elevation or depression, conduction block, or T wave changes (Figure 1). Throughout the clinical course, the echocardiogram demonstrated normal left ventricular function and intracardiac structure, without asynergy. While hospitalization with a high fever sometimes exceeded 40 C, the HR remained between 70 and 100 bpm with a sinus rhythm (Figure 2). The patient was not receiving beta-blocker therapy. In accordance with Cunha's criteria, the patient was diagnosed with relative bradycardia.
On day 6, blood culture was positive for the recovery of B. melitensis identified by mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), and the patient was diagnosed with brucellosis. The patient resided in a part of China (Zhejiang Province) that is not considered endemic for brucellosis.
After being diagnosed with brucellosis, the patient was treated with rifampicin (450 mg qd po) and doxycycline (100 mg bid po) for 6 weeks in accordance with Chinese guidelines. The patient responded to antibiotic treatment without any adverse clinical effects. After treatment, the patient's body temperature returned to normal limits on day 9 and she was discharged from the hospital in stable condition on day 13. At the latest follow-up 3 months after discharge, the patient did not report any symptoms. The whole process was concluded (Figure 3).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 51-year-old female presented with high fevers up to 39.5 °C with chills, cough, headache, diaphoresis, and fatigue for one week.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed high spiking fevers up to 39.5 °C accompanied by shaking chills lasting 20-30 minutes, productive cough, headache, drenching sweats, and fatigue 1 week prior to admission. She presented to the emergency department 5 days prior and was treated with IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily for 2 days; however, temperatures remained refractory (>39-40 °C) with persistent systemic symptoms. She was admitted on May 24, 2021, and noted to have persistent high fevers with relative bradycardia (Faget's sign). Following targeted antimicrobial therapy, defervescence occurred on day 9 with complete recovery.
subjective.past_medical_history: No previous chronic illnesses; prior outpatient treatment with IV ceftriaxone for 2 days. Epidemiological exposure/Occupation: Farmer working with sheep in Zhejiang Province, China.
subjective.review_of_systems: Cough, headache, diaphoresis, and fatigue; denies gastrointestinal symptoms, chest pain, or dyspnea. Home medications: None (not taking beta-blockers). Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vitals: Body temperature 39.1 °C (with fevers exceeding 40.0 °C during hospitalization), heart rate 74-100 beats/min with regular rhythm (relative bradycardia meeting Cunha's criteria in the setting of severe fever). General and systemic physical examination: Unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: WBC 4.25 x 10^9/L (63.7% neutrophils), CRP elevated initially at 8.66 mg/L with marked secondary elevation, elevated serum amyloid A (SAA). Minor-to-moderate elevations of D-dimer, ALT, AST, adenosine deaminase (ADA), serum creatinine, and procalcitonin (PCT). Hepatitis B surface antibody positive. Electrocardiogram (ECG): Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm without arrhythmia, PR interval changes, ST-T abnormalities, or conduction blocks. Transthoracic echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular systolic function and intracardiac structures without regional wall motion abnormalities.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT: Within normal limits without pulmonary infiltrates, consolidation, or lymphadenopathy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Brucellosis presenting with temperature-pulse dissociation (relative bradycardia / Faget's sign), confirmed by blood culture yielding Brucella melitensis identified by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS).
Plan & Clinical Course: Commenced on oral rifampicin 450 mg once daily and oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for a 6-week duration. The patient responded promptly with complete defervescence on hospital day 9, was discharged clinically stable on day 13, and remained fully asymptomatic at 3-month follow-up.
